
Grok social scout found no verifiable primary technical resources. arXiv RSS yielded two moderate-signal candidates: WebGrader (self-evolving programmatic grader for LLM agents on web development tasks, fitting the RLHF-for-agentic-systems pattern) and TRACE (human-AI coordination benchmark under drift/failure, fitting human-in-the-loop evaluation). No other papers from the feed meet 3+ inclusion criteria.

## Suggestions

- [WebGrader: Training LLMs for Web Development with Self-Evolving Programmatic Grader](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06474) — Trains LLM agents on web development tasks using a self-evolving programmatic grader that iteratively refines reward signals from verifiable task outcomes, enabling scalable alignment without manual human annotation at each step.
  Section: Research Papers > RLHF for Agentic Systems | Criteria: Applies reward modeling / verifiable reward learning in an agentic (web development) setting, Goal-directed agent behavior shaped by iteratively refined programmatic reward signals, Iterative alignment loop: self-evolving grader updates reward criteria based on task outcomes, Empirical outcome: task success rate on web development benchmarks

- [TRACE: A Multi-Layer Benchmark for Human AI Controller Coordination Under Drift and Failure](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.06657) — Multi-layer benchmark evaluating human-AI controller coordination in agentic settings subject to distribution drift and failure modes, providing structured evaluation of human-in-the-loop agent alignment.
  Section: Datasets & Benchmarks | Criteria: Human feedback signals shape goal-directed agent behavior in a controller coordination setting, Empirical benchmark with measurable alignment and coordination outcomes, Human-in-the-loop agentic evaluation covering drift and failure scenarios
